question: Does replacing the implied earnings jump with past realized earnings variance create profitable signals?
history: Own-name last 8 completed earnings, minimum 6; fixed close-before to close-after announcement window; subtract two ordinary sessions' past mean squared return; no directional forecast
freeze: latest identifiable reference-only structural fit at or before signal, same upcoming earnings, max 30 calendar days old; no refitting after jump replacement
signal: three sessions before reported earnings; same-day historical data available; threshold relative to signal midpoint
entry: following close, two sessions before earnings; identical trades in midpoint and crossed-spread scenarios
exit: first close after reported earnings date, fixed identities
instruments: closest target-strike ATM straddle and nearest 3 target strikes per call/put at first eligible expiry 8-45 calendar days from signal
hedges: initial reference-IV stock delta held fixed; also report unhedged
costs: midpoint gross; midpoint minus $0.65/contract/side commissions and 2bp/side stock cost; bid/ask crossing plus same commissions/stock cost; no additional option slippage
spread_filter: no relative-spread screen for targets; valid positive signal bid, mid >= $0.25 per leg; record spreads; no exit moneyness filters
aggregation: per-trade premium-normalized result and equal-event averaged result; long/short split; event-cluster bootstrap; do not select winning threshold
limitations: retrospective actual earnings dates, not point-in-time announced schedules
European approximation to US equity options
no funding, borrow, margin, or assignment model
historical P variance inserted into Q model is a trading hypothesis, not true value
expansion: 2021-2024 same five nondividend names; added before inspecting first-panel return summaries; same rules and thresholds; anchor snapshots 15 and 10 sessions before event
actual_public_api_comparison: Also evaluate the delivered MarketSlice hybrid and market-only curves at the signal, plus a jump replacement anchored to the delivered hybrid. Added to directly address current-model threshold request; previous linear-anchor results retained.
